entities.summary:
Indravarman VI, also known as Ba Dich Lai, Chang-pa-ti-lai, Virabhadravarman, or Ngauk Klaung Vijaya, was a king of Champa who ruled from 1400 to 1441. He was crowned in 1432 and took the regnal name Indravarman. Indravarman VI played a significant role in the history of Champa, a kingdom that existed from the 2nd century AD to the 15th century AD. He was a key figure in the politics and economy of Champa during the 15th century AD.

Indravarman VI's reign was marked by several important events, including the expansion of Champa's territory and the establishment of trade relationships with neighboring kingdoms. He also oversaw the construction of several temples and palaces, which were built using local materials and architectural styles.

The legacy of Indravarman VI can be seen in the cultural and historical heritage of Champa. His reign marked the beginning of a new era in Champa's history, characterized by a blend of Indian, Buddhist, and indigenous influences. The temples and palaces built during his reign continue to be an important part of Champa's cultural identity.

The significance of Indravarman VI lies in his role in shaping the course of Champa's history and his contribution to the development of the kingdom's culture and architecture. His legacy continues to be felt in the present day, with many of his temples and palaces remaining an important part of Champa's cultural heritage.
